  Requirement: "Add a default-off RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED guard to both tag-writing release jobs. ... Keep the new behaviour off until a person finishes the operator step: gate it behind `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED` (a feature flag that defaults off, or a placeholder env var that makes the code skip safely). Validate the fix before enabling tagging." (linked issue #7029, second paragraph.)
  Expected change site: `.github/workflows/mark-stable.yml` "Resolve release tagging switch" step env block and the matching step in `.github/workflows/test-and-mark-stable.yml`; the README row for `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED`; the operator paragraph in `changelog.d/7029-release-validate-ci-gate.md`; `tests/test_release_validate_ci_gate.py` `SWITCH_ENV`, `test_tagging_switch_resolution` enabled cases, and any test that asserts the default-on default.
  Evidence of absence: Both workflow resolver steps set `RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED: ${{ vars.RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED || 'true' }}` with default `true` (mark-stable.yml:937, test-and-mark-stable.yml:6626). README.md:247 row reads "default `true`". changelog.d/7029-release-validate-ci-gate.md:9 advertises "default `true`". tests/test_release_validate_ci_gate.py:42 sets `SWITCH_ENV = EXPR_OPEN + " vars.RELEASE_TAGGING_ENABLED || 'true' }}"`, and the resolution test treats unset/`""`/`"true"`/`" TRUE "` as enabled (line 161). The linked issue's "default-off, until a person finishes the operator step" semantic is not honoured: the operator step the issue describes (a human validating the fix before any tag write is enabled) is bypassed by shipping with tagging enabled. Auto-decision AD-2 records a rationale (release jobs already fail closed on CI, default-off would stop every release), but AD-2 is an automated clarify-respond worker choice, not the human review the issue's "Why" paragraph requires; at least three prior autofix iterations have explicitly deferred this gap for the same reason. Honouring the issue verbatim means flipping `|| 'true'` to `|| 'false'` in both resolver env blocks, updating `SWITCH_ENV` and the resolver cases in `test_tagging_switch_resolution`, and amending the README row + changelog paragraph to advertise "default `false`".
